name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 21
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 21

criteria.description: Presence of multisystemic clinical features consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of combined defects in oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activities in muscle or fibroblast samples
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes associated with combined oxidative phosphorylation defects
Neuroimaging evidence of basal ganglia or brainstem abnormalities supportive of mitochondrial disease
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multisystemic clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined oxidative phosphorylation defects and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

searchTerms: progressive muscle weakness and floppy tone
gradual loss of muscle strength and tone
progressive brain damage with slow development

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiencies of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
imaging: MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly factors or structural subunits
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Stroke-like episodes with focal neurological deficits
Onset typically in childhood or adolescence
Characteristic symmetrical necrotic lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem
Specific mitochondrial or nuclear gene mutations

redFlags: Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and sensorineural hearing loss
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
Parikh S, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015.
